text:
maya singh: quick follow-up on the modularization RFC. proposing a "streamlined adapter" playbook to make refactors incremental and low-risk. putting the short plan here.

liam roberts: sounds good. what's different from previous adapter proposals?

maya singh: three refinements: 1) prefer in-process adapters that avoid RPC by default, 2) require a minimal JSON schema for contracts, 3) enforce an adapter TTL + owner label.

sofia garcia: TTL is interesting. how enforced?

maya singh: CI lint forbids new adapters without owner/ttl. infra will auto-create expiry tickets across teams for adapters older than ttl.

liam roberts: perf impact? even in-process hops cost something.
maya singh: internal spike shows median add ~0.25ms using shared-memory adapters. we'll default to binary encoding for hotpaths to cut tail.

sofia garcia: testing strategy?
maya singh: contract-unit tests for each adapter, a contract-smoke run on PR, and selective integration when adapter manifest changes. heavy suites run nightly.

infra-bot: Canary slots available next week. Reserve at infra.internal/canary.

liam roberts: observability?
maya singh: adapters propagate trace context and add contract_id tag. console will get per-contract latency + error rate. alerting if error-rate > 0.3% for 5m.

sofia garcia: rollout phases?
maya singh: phase A: session-coordinator and request-router adapters (4 weeks). phase B: kv-cache gateway + enrichment (8 weeks). full paydown ~4 months.

liam roberts: i'll pair on perf and the binary encoding prototype.

maya singh: thanks. i'll add a short checklist to the RFC doc and open phase A tickets. meeting Fri to lock owners.

sofia garcia: +1, thanks maya.
